questions.q: Why did United States Treasury yields hit a two-year and ten-month high?
o: An oil price surge stoked inflation concerns and rising government debt drove investors toward alternative assets
The Federal Reserve cut benchmark interest rates aggressively to stimulate domestic manufacturing output
Commercial banks flooded the primary market with new liquidity following regulatory changes
Foreign central banks simultaneously dumped their entire holdings of short-term sovereign bills
questions.e: An oil price surge created cost-push pressures while expanding sovereign debt drove institutional capital into hard assets and cryptocurrency. This debasement trade pushed yields higher, whereas rate cuts would lower yields. The other options are not supported by the text.

questions.q: What drove the London Stock Exchange Group to deploy the FTSE 100 on a distributed ledger?
o: It altered settlement mechanics, fractional asset access, and collateral mobility using blockchain architecture
Regulatory authorities mandated that all primary benchmark indices trade exclusively on decentralized exchanges
Commercial lenders sought to eliminate overnight interbank lending rates through smart contracts
Retail investors demanded the complete removal of all traditional custodian institutions
questions.e: The partnership with Kraken deployed the benchmark on a blockchain architecture, directly altering settlement mechanics, fractional asset access, and collateral mobility. Regulatory mandates or retail demands are absent from the text. Interbank lending rates are not mentioned in this context.

questions.q: Why did the DIW institute upgrade its German economic growth forecasts?
o: Export figures and foreign sales momentum surpassed consensus expectations, providing a buffer against domestic industrial contraction
The central bank lowered reserve requirements for commercial lenders operating in domestic manufacturing
Energy costs fell sharply across European industrial centers to historical lows
Government subsidies replaced local capital formation figures entirely
questions.e: External demand and export prints that exceeded consensus expectations provided a buffer against local industrial slowdowns. Lower reserve requirements or energy costs falling are not mentioned in the source text. Domestic capital formation was actually weak rather than replaced by subsidies.

questions.q: What caused the Japanese yen to trade below 157.80 against the dollar?

Foreign institutional investors accelerated their purchases of domestic equities through local trading houses
Commercial banks increased their foreign fixed-income allocations to capture wider yield differentials
questions.e: The appreciation stemmed from an aggressive repricing of Bank of Japan policy, softer Federal Reserve commentary, and the unwinding of carry positions amid intervention risks. Buying foreign fixed income or domestic equities would weaken the yen rather than strengthen it.

Government spending programs entirely replaced manufacturing output with state-backed infrastructure projects.

questions.q: Why did Japanese institutional allocators trim their overseas bond holdings for a second consecutive week?

Foreign central banks banned domestic institutions from holding cross-border debt instruments.

Japanese regulators imposed strict capital controls forbidding any foreign fixed-income exposure.

questions.e: Broad dollar depreciation driven by yen dynamics created upward pressure on the yuan, taking it to a three-and-a-half-year high. Capital controls were not abolished, and the Fed does not intervene in Shanghai currency markets.
